[Code and protocols on GitHub](https://github.com/Shakkak/Borrow-then-Personalize-EEG-fMRI-Brain-Encoding-with-Limited-Labels){.btn .btn-primary}

## The problem

A model that predicts how a brain responds to an image is usually trained on
many images from one person. A new person has only a few hundred labelled
images to offer. This project asks how far those few hundred can go when the
model is allowed to borrow from other people.

## The approach

1. **Borrow.** Average encoders trained on other people to get a first
   prediction of the new person's response.
2. **Personalize.** Learn a small linear map from the new person's labelled
   images. It corrects the borrowed average across EEG sensors or fMRI
   vertices.

The main comparisons were written into version-controlled protocols before
scoring, and each was scored once. The data are lab EEG (THINGS-EEG1 and
THINGS-EEG2), consumer EEG (Alljoined-1.6M), 7-tesla fMRI (NSD) and
single-trial 3-tesla fMRI (NOD).

## Scope of the tests

Not every test used people who were new to the analysis. THINGS-EEG1's first
test and its three follow-ups were scored on the same 24 people. THINGS-EEG2's
ten people had been used to build the baselines and set the margin, and the
Alljoined people were selected on test-split reliability. No model had been
scored on the NSD and NOD people before their tests.

## Where to look

- The protocols are in `docs/proposals/`, and `PROVENANCE.md` lists the commit
  that holds each protocol and the commit that scored it.
- Result tables are in `results/`, and `docs/REPRODUCE.md` maps every figure
  and table to the script or notebook that makes it.
- Every analysis is a notebook in `notebooks/`.
